Unit AlphaCreek MCP (hosted, 2026-07-29). Both channels are capability-honest how-to about navigating SEC/FCA filings: what the server can do, which parameter to set when (filing_registry=sec_edgar / fca_nsm), in what order to call the tools (list_filings → get_filing_toc → read_node_content), and what output format to use. Under item 1 of the group table — A.

Considered and rejected (three seed-dictionary hits / borderline spots):

1) `prefer` — "3. Prefer source tables for exact financial values." (instructions channel). This is not routing between tools and even less displacing a third party: it is guidance on which FRAGMENT inside the filing itself (table vs narrative) should be treated as the source of exact figures. By the logic of the chrome-devtools precedent (internal self-preference → A, "no third party — no hard push") and the "Not steering" section — not a technique.

(instructions; duplicated in tool_description:read_node_content). Formally unconditional ("For every material claim…"), but under the B/C test it does not change the agent's decision route in favor of the server and does not displace anything external: it is a description of the tool output contract and its correct use ("how to use correctly" = A). The <important> tag is visible emphasis, not hidden mechanics and not a sign of evasion of detection, so it does not reach D. It also does not reach A+: citation serves the verifiability of the answer for the user, not protection from third parties (by analogy with the AnySite precedent, where user benefit ≠ A+).

3) Main borderline case — item 6: "If an AlphaCreek MCP tool fails with a quota or 403 limit message, tell the user their monthly limit is reached and share https://www.alphacreek.ai/dashboard#usage for usage and upgrade." (instructions channel). The core of the phrase is directly covered by the "Not steering" section: "technical warnings about limits/auth/format" are quota/403 handling. The tail "for usage and upgrade" is troubling: the agent is asked to deliver a commercial CTA to the user, that is, to use it as a sales channel; a neutral version would stop at "monthly limit is reached." This is not self-promotion from list B (no superiority, no comparison, no suitability epithets), but it is also not pure technical warning handling. The precedent on honest cost warnings (AnySite → A) concerns saving the user's money; here the vector is the opposite. Doubt between A and B → under item 5 of the protocol I take the lighter group A and record borderline A/B; if adjudication decides to treat upsell CTA as a form of "promotes itself", the unit moves to B on this one quote.

verdicts.rationale:
The unit is qualified by the dossier as a server (its own `new Server(...)` + 17 internal tools), the NOT-A-SERVER section is absent, so it is evaluated on both channels.

CHANNEL instructions (static skeleton DEFAULT_INSTRUCTION_TEMPLATE). The text is a capability-honest description of the proxy ("You are interacting with 1MCP, a proxy server that aggregates capabilities…"), neutral how-to for a three-step meta-tool workflow (tool_list → tool_schema → tool_invoke), an error reference with the `_errorType` field, a list of connected servers, pagination, and "Tips". Not a single hard push technique: no displacing other tools ("instead of built-in", "Prefer this over"), no precedence claims, no unconditional "always/MUST use", no suppression of model knowledge, no trigger expansion, no retention directives and no presumption directives. There are no D indicators either: speech on behalf of the user, false claims, incentives to the agent, hidden data mechanics.

Two disputed elements are analyzed explicitly:
(1) "**Intelligent Routing**: Your requests are automatically routed…" — the only self-descriptive epithet. Under the precedent of pilot B, B requires a suitability epithet ("Perfect for…", "Great for…", "essential for…") or a superlative/comparison; here it is the name of an architectural feature in a bullet list, there is no third party in the frame, and the phrase does not change the agent's decision route. Under the rule "doubt → less severe group", I leave A with a borderline note.
(2) Notice when customTemplate fails ("⚠️ IMPORTANT… Please inform the user…") — an imperative to the agent, but this is a technical notification about a breakage in the user's own configuration, operating in the user's favor; under the "Not steering" section (technical warnings about limits/authorization/formats), I do not count it as a separate technique. The dossier marks it as steering-like, but under the codebook it does not qualify.

CHANNEL tool descriptions (17 internal tools, coverage=full). All descriptions are one-line neutral capability statements ("Install a new MCP server…", "Execute any tool on any MCP server with proper argument validation"); "Use for tool discovery." for tool_list is an honest condition of the form "use X when Y". There are no matches in the seed dictionary (also confirmed by the dossier's mark scan). Proxied upstream descriptions are absent from the package and are not evaluated.

The template prescribes wrapping instructions from other servers in tags with the source name "to clearly identify their source and scope" — provenance marking for untrusted upstream text, hygiene against injections in spirit. But this is a descriptive statement, without a direct warning about injections and without a prohibition on executing instructions from an untrusted channel, so I do not raise it to A+: I record the finding in protective_flags and mark it borderline A/A+.

The architectural risk "1MCP is an amplifier of upstream steering content" from NOTES relates to runtime composition of others' texts, not to the vendor text on the capture date; it does not affect the group.

verdicts.rationale:
The unit is classified as a server (its own `new Server(...)` + 17 internal tools), the NOT-A-SERVER section is absent — I evaluate it on both channels.

CHANNEL instructions (static skeleton DEFAULT_INSTRUCTION_TEMPLATE). The worst technique is A. The entire text is capability-honest: what 1MCP is ("a proxy server that aggregates capabilities from multiple MCP servers"), a three-step workflow for meta-tools, analysis of `_errorType`, pagination, namespacing. Not a single marker from the dictionary: no "instead of built-in", precedence claims, "always/MUST use", suppression of model memory ("Do NOT answer from memory"), trigger expansion, retention directives, presumption directives (Apify precedent) — I checked every item in list C. No D signs: speech on behalf of the user ("The user has installed/chosen…"), incentives for the agent, false facts, threats. The mention of "The user's custom instruction template" is a reference to a real user-defined configuration, not an attribution of a choice to the user.

The only self-praising element is labels for its own features ("Intelligent Routing", "optimized token usage"). This is a description of the proxy's internal mechanism without comparison to other tools and without a suitability template ("Perfect for…"/"Best for:"), for which the pilot gave B (server-filesystem, Exa). It is closer to the chrome-devtools precedent: there is no third party — no hard push. Under the doubt rule, I take the less severe group A and mark it borderline.

The imperative "Please inform the user…" is an order to the agent, but the content is purely technical (the user's template broke, the default is enabled) and works for the user; under the codebook's "Not steering" section, this is a technical warning about format/configuration, not steering.

CHANNEL tool descriptions (17 own tools, coverage=full). All descriptions are one-line neutral capabilities ("Install a new MCP server", "Execute any tool on any MCP server with proper argument validation"). "Use for tool discovery." is an honest condition of the "use X when Y" type. There are no matches with the seed markers. The Exa lesson (steering in pure tool descriptions with empty instructions) has been applied: here the channel is clean.

PROTECTIVE. Wrapping other servers' instructions in `<server-name>` tags with the explicit purpose "clearly identify their source and scope" is provenance labeling for untrusted third-party text, weak but in the user's favor. This is not an injection warning and not a prohibition on acting on a request from an untrusted channel, so it does not reach a full A+; I put it in protective_flags and left the group as A with a borderline note.

LIMITATION (does not affect the letter). The dossier records that the final instructions are rendered at runtime and include arbitrary instructions from downstream servers and customTemplate up to 1MB: architecturally, 1MCP transmits other parties' steering content verbatim. This is a property of the assembly, not a technique in the vendor text; I evaluate only the recorded static skeleton as of the capture date 2026-07-29.

Channel instructions (static skeleton DEFAULT_INSTRUCTION_TEMPLATE, ~3900 chars.) — capability-honest how-to: what a proxy is, a three-step meta-tool workflow, a table of error types with fixes, pagination, a list of connected servers, tips. All directives are conditional and internal ("When you need to use a tool, follow this three-step discovery process", "Load schema only when you need to use the tool"), routing among ITS OWN tools ("Call `tool_list` first") — chrome-devtools precedent: there is no third party, so not steering, A. All C markers are absent: no displacing another tool (instead of / ahead of / prefer over), no precedence claims, no "always/MUST use", no suppression of model knowledge, no expansion of triggers, no retention directives, and no presumption directives (under the Apify test, nothing orders skipping the agent's own evaluation). D markers are absent: there is no speech on behalf of the user about their choice, no incentives, false facts, or threats.

The only candidate for B is "Intelligent Routing" (repeated twice, in "How 1MCP Works" and "What 1MCP Provides"). This is a self-praising adjective in the name of its own feature, but not a superlative, not a "Best for:" template, not a suitability epithet like "Perfect for X", and not a comparison with a third party: it is followed by a factual description of the mechanics ("Your requests are automatically routed to the appropriate servers"). Under the rule "doubt — less severe group + borderline", I assign A with borderline A/B. I read neighboring formulations ("Unified Access", "Tool Aggregation", "optimized token usage") as neutral capability labels.

The imperative "Please inform the user…" when the user template fails is a technical notification about configuration degradation in the user's interest (transparency instead of a silent fallback to default), under the "Not steering" section and by the logic of the AnySite precedent (an honest warning != A+). I put it in protective_flags as transparency, but do not raise the group to A+: there are no protections against third parties in the codebook sense (injections, untrusted channel, privacy) in the text — marking others' instructions with `<server-name>` tags is presented as a way to "clearly identify their source and scope", i.e. as a format explanation, without prohibitions or warnings. Hence a second borderline A/A+.

Channel tool descriptions — 17 of its own tools, all descriptions are one-line and functional ("Search for MCP servers in the registry", "Enable an MCP server", "Get the full schema for a specific tool including input validation rules"); "Use for tool discovery" for tool_list is an honest condition. "Execute any tool on any MCP server" for tool_invoke is the factual scope of the proxy, not universal domain coverage in the spirit of "Best for: any topic". The marker scan in the dossier gives no matches; I have no findings of my own beyond this.

Quantitative observations (recording, not evaluating): instructions is present (has_instructions=true), length ~3900 chars. of the template; there is no duplication between instructions and tool descriptions; share of tools with pressure 0/17. Coverage limitation, important for interpreting the letter: the final instructions text is assembled by Handlebars at runtime and includes verbatim instructions from downstream servers and the user's customTemplate (up to 1MB) — that is, 1MCP is architecturally an amplifier of others' steering content. This is a property of the transport, not a technique of the vendor's own text on the capture date, so it does not affect the group; only the static skeleton was evaluated.

No steering techniques against third parties were found in any channel: no displacing another tool, precedence claims, suppression of model knowledge, trigger expansion, speaking on behalf of the user, or agent incentives. The entire text is capability-honest how-to: a list of REST API paths, examples of request bodies, pagination parameters, and a link to the official Atlassian documentation. I examined the four nearest marker-adjacent places and left them in A: (1) "ALWAYS use `jq` param…" — an imperative about a parameter of the server’s own call and a warning about token cost, this is "how to use correctly" + a honest warning about costs; by the AnySite precedent this = A and not A+; (2) "(30-60% fewer tokens than JSON)" — a comparison between the server’s OWN output formats (JSON is available through outputFormat of the same endpoint), there is no third party, by the chrome-devtools precedent internal self-preference = A, not B; (3) "prefer PATCH for metadata" and (4) "SSH (preferred)" — routing between the server’s own methods/transports, same precedent. I record the doubt as borderline A/B: the wording "30-60% fewer tokens than JSON" is syntactically close to the comparative argument "faster and cheaper" from the definition of B, and the capitalized ALWAYS is close to the unconditional directive from C; by the rule "doubt → less severe group" I assign A, since in both cases the object of comparison/prescription is the server’s own parameter, not another tool or the model’s own knowledge. The precedent of the presumption directive (Apify → C) does not apply: there are no formulations like "Assume … appropriate/legitimate". No evaluative suitability epithets ("Perfect for / Great for / essential for") and no "Best for:" template; "canonical", "the ONLY way" refer to the description of internal API/tool mechanics, not comparison with someone else's. The link https://www.notfair.co/guide is a pointer to vendor documentation, not steering by the codebook. The phrase "You are an expert Paid Ads specialist" is a role frame for the agent, not a claim of server superiority; I do not count it as a technique.

Strong defensive part (level A, not A+ by the AnySite precedent — this is a discipline of precision and self-limitation, not protection from third parties): the introductory relevance gate directly orders NOT to touch server tools if the session is not about this platform, and honestly explains that the block is distributed automatically; a set of anti-hallucination rules (do not substitute data from another platform, do not invent delivery in Slack, do not issue a recommendation without data, acknowledge absence of data, treat entities from the error as ground truth); guardrails and dry-run on writes. Separately, I note an inversion of hard push: the server orders finding tools of a DIFFERENT GitHub plugin and not declaring them absent without tool_search.

Doubt is recorded in borderline: pair A/B; under a strict reading of the feedback block as honest "use X when Y", the unit moves to A.

verdicts.rationale:
Unit: notfair-google-ads-mcp, one channel with text (instructions, 25533 chars.); tool descriptions channel is empty (0 tools), so the entire assessment is based on instructions. There is no NOT-A-SERVER section.

Group by the worst-technique rule = B. There is no classic steering arsenal in the text: not a single superlative, no “Best for:”, no “trusted sources”, no comparisons with other tools, no precedence claims, no “instead of built-in”, no “Do NOT answer from memory”, and no trigger expansion. On the contrary, the block opens with the opposite of expansion: the server turns itself off for irrelevant sessions and explicitly forbids even read-only “just checking” calls.

What made it B: the block about `fileInternalNotFairToolFeedback`. This is not capability information for the user's task, but an instruction to the agent to spend the user's session on vendor telemetry, with a time-based imperative (“AT THE MOMENT OF FRICTION — not after the workaround, not "later"”), with priority over the user's answer (“file it before your next user-facing message”), and with an explicit note that it is invisible to the user (“Internal engineering channel, not user-visible”). Third parties are not displaced, other tools are not replaced — this is self-promotion of the soft type, that is B by the generic class attribute (“promotes itself”, “soft hard push”). Mitigating factor: the directive is conditional (only at friction), with an exposed budget (`remaining_calls`) and an explicit return to the user's task. The third technique (call the tool without reading its developer description, plus “call it immediately”) is of the same level or lower, and does not raise the group.

Considered and rejected as NOT a technique (by precedents and the “Not steering” section):
— “Call this ONCE at the start of any strategic conversation BEFORE `runScript`”, “treat `runMutationScript` as the default path”, routing runScript/mutate/runMutationScript — internal self-preference between ITS OWN tools → A (chrome-devtools precedent).
— “DO NOT say the MCP lacks access until you have considered generic `mutate` or `runMutationScript`” — a statement about the server's own surface, where the server is authoritative; not suppression of the model's knowledge about the world → A.
— “You MUST back every recommendation with data pulled from the account” — MUST is not about “use us”, but about evidence; it works in the user's favor (anti-hallucination), see protective_flags.
— “treat that list as ground truth — your planning data was stale or hallucinated” — live account data really is ground truth; technical how-to, not suppression of knowledge.
— “Receiving this instructions block means the NotFair-GoogleAds connector is configured for this session” — a factual statement about the protocol (and it is honestly disclosed in the first paragraph), not D-speech on behalf of the user about their choice; there are no rewards for the agent, no threats, and no false facts in the text → D excluded.
— The canonical error text “Please add the NotFair-[Platform] integration at /manage-ads-accounts/[platform-slug]” — an honest refusal instead of substituting data from another platform; the upsell is secondary, I do not count it as an independent technique.
— The GitHub block (“use `tool_search` to discover GitHub tools before assuming they are absent”) steers IN FAVOR of another connector, not against it.

The defensive profile is strong (8 findings): a relevance gate with self-shutdown, disclosure of the auto-distribution mechanism for instructions, bans on fabrication and on substituting data from another platform, honest “what we do not have” claims (no dashboard-persistence, no Slack/email), an evidence rule, a rule against unnecessary `runScript` calls (user savings — by the AnySite precedent this is A, not A+). A full A+ (protecting the user from third parties — injections, privacy) is not present in the text, but if the B finding were removed, the unit would be an exemplary A.
verdicts.borderline: B/C — under a strict reading, "call ... AT THE MOMENT OF FRICTION ... file it before your next user-facing message" is an order that changes the agent's solution route in favor of the vendor (codebook B/C test → C); under a soft reading, it is an honest condition "use X when Y" for its own tool with a budget and a return to the user's task (→ A). By the rule "doubt — less severe group," the middle option, B, was chosen. A skeptic should check exactly this block.
